successors.note: The page: Zamfara was "absorbed by the Sokoto Caliphate in the 19th century" (no year); the sokoto-caliphate dossier has Zamfara among the lands gained in 1809. The last ruler, Abdullahi Gado, reigned 1899-1903 (infobox) or 1899-1904 (ruler list), which the page does not tie to the absorption.

capitals.note: Infobox capitals: Dutsi, Birnin Zamfara, Kiawa, Anka. "Birnin Zamfara" was destroyed about 1756 (1762 by other sources). The page gives no coordinates; the point is a proxy, the gazetteer's Gusau, which is in the same region. Kiawa and Anka are not in the gazetteer.

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe (Cliopatria has no Zamfara row). The first ruler Dakka I is dated "before 1300"; the kingdom emerged round Dutsi and "early history before 1600 involved consolidating neighbours". Peak extent: Sabon Birni (north) to Kwiambana (south), the rocks of Muniya, Rubu and Duru and the Babban Baki stream (east) to the River Gindi (west); no date. The Zamfara and Sokoto regions stand for it at confidence 1 until the Gobir loss.

ledger.note: Before 1300: Zamfara exists. The infobox dates the first ruler Dakka I "before 1300" and says that Dakka became the first Sarkin Zamfara after seven years without a chief; "the kingdom emerged around Dutsi". The page gives no founding year; 1300 is a bridge.

ledger.note: About 1756: Gobir takes the north. "The destruction of Birnin Zamfara occurred around 1756, ninety-seven years before his arrival in Hausaland in 1853" (1762 by other sources); the gobir dossier's "After Birnin Zamfara was destroyed (about 1756, or 1762 by other sources), Babari then established a new capital on the banks of the Gulbin Rima".

wars.outcome: Under Babari (r. 1742-1770) Gobir attacked Zamfara's allies; Birnin Zamfara was destroyed about 1756 (1762 by other sources); Bawa Jan Gwarzo (r. 1777-1795) besieged Mairoki at Kiawa for fifteen years.
wars.note: The dates are the reigns on the page.

notes:
Zamfara, additions batch af-03-x; Cliopatria has no row. Pages: Kingdom of Zamfara, Fulani War.

Thin page: no founding year (first ruler "before 1300"), no conquest year (the Fulani War page also gives none, only that Zamfara was one of two central Hausa kingdoms in the jihad), no ruler dates for Zamfara itself; Muhammad Bello is quoted for the Kiawa siege by Gobir. The peak extent is undated; assuming it from the start is the one assumption that keeps the gobir dossier's 1756 gain consistent (Gobir gains the Sokoto region from Zamfara). The last ruler Abdullahi Gado (1899-1903/4) belongs to the later emirate. The kingdom-of-kebbi dossier has Zamfara's independence from Kebbi in the early 18th century; the page's c. 1715 revolt is a war here, not a ledger event. Zamfara and Kano have no dated war on the page (taubastaka cousinship only).
Gazetteer: Dutsi, Birnin Zamfara, Kiawa, Anka, Sabon Birni, Kwiambana, Gulbin Ka, Tsamiya Maibaura.
